summary: Reddit and Bluesky were blocked today, so this report rests on Hacker News threads and Apple Developer Forum posts. Two themes stand out: Indian developers locked out of the Apple Developer Program with no explanation, and a wave of people trying to leave Google after its Gmail/Photos ad-targeting announcement and finding Takeout painful.

ideas.title: Apple Enrollment Unblock Kit for India
ideas.oneLiner: A guided checklist, case tracker and escalation-letter generator for developers in India whose Apple Developer Program enrollment is blocked or declined.
ideas.problem: Individual developers in India hit an immediate "Unable to Continue" error or a templated decline with no reason and no appeal path. Support cases sit unanswered for weeks, and every forum thread ends the same way, so each person re-discovers the same dead ends alone.
ideas.targetUsers: Indian indie developers and returning NRIs who want to publish iOS apps as individuals.
ideas.monetization: Free guide and tracker for reach; ₹499 one-time for the escalation pack (letter templates, evidence checklist, org/D-U-N-S route walkthrough) or a small paid concierge review.
mvp: Diagnostic questionnaire (Apple ID region history, ID match, 2FA, entity type) that points to likely causes
Case log with dates, case ID and follow-up reminders
Escalation email and letter generator for Developer Support, Developer Relations and the App Store Connect contact form
Crowd-sourced anonymous outcome board: what finally worked and how long it took
Alternate-route guide: enrolling as an organisation with a D-U-N-S number, and shipping Android first while waiting

competitors.name: Apple Developer Forums
competitors.gap: Threads pile up with no staff resolution and no consolidated, searchable answer on what actually worked.

competitors.name: Apple Developer Support contact form
competitors.gap: Posters report the email option disappearing, templated rejections and no reasons given.

sources.title: Comment on an Apple developer program thread
sources.quote: I lived in the US for about 10 years and moved back to India this year. My Apple Account was set to the US region and I switched it to India before enrolling in the Apple Developer Program as an individual. I verified with my passport and paid with an Indian card. The enrollment was declined.

ideas.title: Takeout Mover for Huge Google Libraries
ideas.oneLiner: A resumable desktop tool that pulls a large Google Photos/Drive library straight to Immich, Ente or a local disk with metadata intact, no multi-day Takeout waits.
ideas.problem: After Google said it may use Gmail and Photos data for ad targeting, many people want out. Takeout is slow, archives expire, and hundreds of gigabytes are close to impossible to download reliably, so people fall back on rclone and community scripts.
ideas.targetUsers: People with hundreds of GB of Google Photos who want to move to Immich, Ente or a NAS but are not comfortable with the command line.
ideas.monetization: One-time licence (about $29) with a free tier capped at a few GB; optional paid managed migration for families.
mvp: Google sign-in, then chunked and resumable downloads with progress and retries
Merge the metadata JSON back into EXIF (dates, GPS, albums)
One-click targets: local folder, Immich upload, Ente import-ready folder
Verification report: counts, hashes and a list of files that failed or were duplicated
Optional schedule so the copy runs overnight

competitors.name: Google Takeout
competitors.gap: Archives take days to prepare, expire, and are painful to download at the hundreds-of-GB scale.

competitors.name: immich-go
competitors.gap: Command-line only and Immich-specific; it works well for people who can use a terminal.

competitors.name: rclone
competitors.gap: Powerful but needs setup and does not restore photo metadata for you.

ideas.title: Google Exit Planner
ideas.oneLiner: A step-by-step planner that maps every Google service you use to a replacement and tracks the accounts still tied to your Gmail address until you can leave.
ideas.problem: People want to leave Google but do not know where to start: which alternative fits each service, how to move contacts and mail, and how to find every account that uses their Gmail address. Switching to a custom domain is described as a huge pain.
ideas.targetUsers: Privacy-minded non-experts and families moving off Gmail, Docs and Photos.
ideas.monetization: Free planner; $5 per month or $39 per year for the account-discovery scan, reminders and migration checklists, plus affiliate links to alternative providers.
mvp: Service-by-service questionnaire (Mail, Docs, Photos, Calendar, Maps, Android) with recommended replacements
Generated migration checklist with order of operations and a rollback plan
Account discovery: paste or upload sender domains from an email export to list services using your Gmail address
Custom-domain email setup guide with forwarding templates
Progress tracker with weekly reminders

competitors.name: switching.software
competitors.gap: A static list of alternatives with no personalised plan, no progress tracking and no account discovery.

competitors.name: Proton
competitors.gap: Offers import tools for its own products only; it does not plan a whole-Google exit.

ideas.title: Personal Outage Alert for Banks and Fintech
ideas.oneLiner: A mobile app that pings you when the banks, UPI apps and SaaS tools you actually use are failing, ahead of the provider's own status page.
ideas.problem: When a bank or fintech app goes down, users learn about it from Reddit or by getting stuck at checkout, and official status pages and notifications lag behind. People want a proactive heads-up that their card or app is affected.
ideas.targetUsers: Heavy UPI and card users, travellers and freelancers who depend on a handful of financial apps.
ideas.monetization: Free for 3 services; ₹49 per month for unlimited services, SMS/WhatsApp alerts and a family plan.
mvp: Pick your banks, UPI apps and SaaS tools from a catalogue
Synthetic checks plus aggregated Downdetector-style signals to detect outages early
Push alert with plain wording: what is down and what still works
Fallback suggestions, such as another UPI app or card
Outage history per service

competitors.name: Downdetector
competitors.gap: A website to check, not a personalised proactive alert tied to the services you use.

competitors.name: StatusGator
competitors.gap: Aimed at teams that monitor SaaS vendors, and it relies on official status pages that users say lag.
